Good evening, readers! Take a quick break and catch up on today's top headlines across India, global affairs, entertainment, and sports.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday for his second visit to India this year and is scheduled to hold bilateral talks with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar. The two sides are expected to discuss strengthening cooperation in defence, security, technology and critical minerals amid continuing strains in bilateral ties. Read more here
Model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and driver Tanveer Ali alias Danish were arrested in Nagpur on Tuesday by a joint team of Lucknow Police and Uttar Pradesh STF in connection with cafe owner Shiva Sharma’s death. Sharma, 28, died after falling from the fourth floor of an apartment building in Lucknow on October 9. His mother filed a murder complaint against Dubey and others, and the allegations are under investigation. Read more here
Cockroach Janata Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on Tuesday moved the Delhi High Court challenging the Special Executive Magistrate’s order extending their custody by two days. The petition was filed in the afternoon through advocate Abhik Chimni. Read more here
Ranbir Kapoor surprised fans by addressing them in Telugu at the Hyderabad event for Ramayana: Rise of a Legend on Monday. The actor, who plays Lord Rama in Nitesh Tiwari’s upcoming film, received loud cheers for his effort, while co-star Sai Pallavi, who plays Sita, watched with a smile. The event was held ahead of the film’s theatrical release in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, where it will be distributed by Dil Raju’s Sri Venkateswara Creations. Read more here
Erik ten Hag and Cristiano Ronaldo’s fallout was one of Manchester United’s most talked-about issues during the 2022-23 season, drawing attention away from the team’s declining performances. The public dispute began after Ronaldo was substituted at half-time during a pre-season friendly against Rayo Vallecano and left the stadium before the final whistle, upsetting then-manager Ten Hag. Operating round the clock, the desk brings together experienced editors, reporters and correspondents to deliver fast, accurate and contextual reporting across subjects that influence public policy, governance, business, society and international affairs. The HT News Desk covers politics, elections, government policies, the economy, business and markets, science and technology, the environment, law and order, infrastructure, education, climate issues and geopolitics, while closely tracking developments across states, institutions and global capitals. The team also leads coverage of major breaking news events, policy announcements, court proceedings, natural disasters, public emergencies and significant international developments. Reports published by the newsdesk are based on information gathered from reporters on the ground, official statements, government agencies, court records, regulatory filings, recognised institutions and other authoritative sources. Stories undergo editorial scrutiny and verification processes to ensure accuracy, fairness and relevance, and are updated as events evolve and additional information becomes available. Whether covering a key political decision in New Delhi, an economic policy shift affecting millions, a landmark court ruling or a major global event, the HT News Desk aims to provide readers with reliable, fact-based journalism that delivers not only the latest developments but also the context and analysis needed to understand their wider implications.
